name: Sofosbuvir
drug_class: HCV NS5B polymerase inhibitor (nucleotide analogue prodrug)
route_note: oral tablet (or pellets) once daily for 8–24 weeks, alone or in fixed-dose combinations
targets: Hepatitis C virus NS5B RNA-dependent RNA polymerase
originator: Pharmasset (Michael Sofia and colleagues); developed by Gilead Sciences
owner: Gilead Sciences; generics in many low- and middle-income countries

discovery.note: Phosphoramidate ProTide prodrug of a 2'-fluoro-2'-C-methyluridine monophosphate, designed to be activated in the liver.

tagline: Pangenotypic backbone of hepatitis C cures, famous for its $84,000 price
summary: Sofosbuvir is a nucleotide analogue that inhibits the hepatitis C virus polymerase and is active against all genotypes. In combinations such as ledipasvir/sofosbuvir and sofosbuvir/velpatasvir it cures more than 95% of patients with a short, interferon-free oral course. Its US launch price of $84,000 for 12 weeks set off a global debate about drug pricing.
mechanism: Sofosbuvir is a ProTide prodrug taken up by the liver, where cathepsin A or carboxylesterase 1 and histidine triad nucleotide-binding protein 1 release the monophosphate. Cellular kinases form the active uridine triphosphate analogue (GS-461203).

The active triphosphate is incorporated by the HCV NS5B polymerase and acts as a chain terminator. Because the NS5B active site is highly conserved, sofosbuvir works against all HCV genotypes and has a very high barrier to resistance (S282T confers reduced susceptibility but is rare).
uses: Chronic hepatitis C (all genotypes) in adults and children aged 3 years and older, in combination with other antivirals
Hepatitis C in compensated and, with some combinations, decompensated cirrhosis
Hepatitis C before and after liver transplantation

history.title: Acquisition
history.detail: Gilead acquires Pharmasset for about $11 billion.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Sovaldi is approved in December 2013 at a list price of $84,000 for a 12-week course.

history.title: Harvoni and access deals
history.detail: Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir becomes the first all-oral, interferon-free single tablet for genotype 1; Gilead signs licences with Indian generic makers for low-income countries.

history.title: Pangenotypic
history.detail: Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir (Epclusa) is approved as the first pangenotypic single-tablet regimen.

history.title: Class boxed warning
history.detail: The FDA adds a boxed warning on hepatitis B reactivation to all direct-acting HCV antivirals.

history.title: Authorised generics
history.detail: Gilead's subsidiary Asegua launches lower-priced authorised generics of Epclusa and Harvoni in the US.

pk.half_life: sofosbuvir about 0.4 h; main circulating metabolite GS-331007 about 27 h
pk.bioavailability: well absorbed; not affected meaningfully by food
pk.metabolism: hepatic activation to the triphosphate; dephosphorylation to inactive GS-331007

serious: hepatitis B reactivation in co-infected patients
symptomatic bradycardia when combined with amiodarone
safety.boxed_warning: Risk of hepatitis B virus reactivation, sometimes fulminant, in patients co-infected with HCV and HBV; test for HBV before starting (US label).

facts: The price of Sovaldi (often quoted as $1,000 per pill) prompted a US Senate investigation in 2015.
Egypt used generic sofosbuvir-based regimens in a national programme that treated millions of people.
WHO's goal of eliminating hepatitis C as a public health threat by 2030 relies heavily on sofosbuvir-based regimens.
